history.period: 12th century CE (present structure); origins claimed to 5th century BCE (unverified)
history.summary: Nagara-style temple dedicated to Rukmini, chief queen of Krishna and an incarnation of Lakshmi, about 2 km from the Dwarkadhish Temple. The present structure dates to the 12th century CE, built under Solanki patronage, though local tradition traces worship here to ancient times. The site is tied to the Durvasa legend: the sage cursed Rukmini to live apart from Krishna, which is why her shrine stands away from the main Krishna temple. Local belief holds that a Dwarka pilgrimage is complete only after darshan here. NOTE: Wikipedia's infobox lists completion as '19th century' while its article text says the present form is 12th century - CONFLICT (verify). The sanctum houses a marble four-armed Rukmini holding shankha, chakra, gada and padma; the temple is known for its jal daan (water offering) custom.

name: Rukmini Devi Temple
town_description: Dwarka is an ancient coastal city in western Gujarat on the Arabian Sea, revered as the legendary capital of Krishna's kingdom and one of the four Char Dham pilgrimage sites. The Dwarkadhish Temple, dedicated to Krishna as the king of Dwarka, dominates the skyline with a 43-metre shikhara. The city draws millions of pilgrims each year and is also the gateway to Bet Dwarka island and the Nageshwar Jyotirlinga.
